extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of classical geometry / mathematicians interested in Archimedean results
extracted.subtask_description: A translation/excerpt of Archimedes' treatises on conoids, spheroids and spirals containing propositions, constructions, definitions and proofs (Propositions 1–19 of On Spirals and several spheroid/conoid results). Useful as a reference for classical geometric constructions and ratio results for spheroidal segments and the arithmetic and geometric properties of the Archimedean spiral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equality of segment ABB' to cone V (existence/uniqueness proof)
rubrics_metrics.description: If V is a cone (or segment of a cone) chosen so that V : (cone or segment of cone ABB') = HD : A'D, then the segment ABB' is equal to V. The proof proceeds by assuming inequality (greater or less), inscribing/circumscribing cylinders/frusta and comparing sums of component volumes/areas to reach contradiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Archimedes constructs inscribed and circumscribed figures made of equal cylinders/frusta, compares corresponding parts via gnomons and rectangles, uses limits/inequalities (Prop. 1, Prop. 2 / Lemma arguments) and shows neither greater nor less is possible, hence equality. This is an existence-and-uniqueness style constructive proof using exhaustion (inscribed/circumscribed approximations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Special case: segment equal to half-spheroid ratio 2:1
rubrics_metrics.description: When the segment is half the spheroid (distance CD or c/2 vanishes), the segment ABB' bears to the cone (or segment of cone ABB') the ratio 2 : 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This follows by the vanishing of certain terms in the general ratio and use of the Lemma to Prop. 2 (On Spirals, Prop. 10) producing the ratio 3:2 in an intermediate step; substituting CA for AD in a general formula also yields the same result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propositions 31–32: ratio for spheroid cut by a plane
rubrics_metrics.description: If a plane divides a spheroid into two unequal segments and AN, A'N are the axes of the lesser and greater segments respectively (C is centre), then (greater segment) : (cone or segment of cone with same base and axis) = (CA + AN) : AN (i.e., (segment A'PP') : (cone A'PP') = CA + AN : AN).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction involves tangents to the elliptic section, drawing planes parallel to base, constructing cones with vertices at A and A' with specified bases, and composing a chain of proportionalities between cones, segments and spheroid (using earlier Propositions 27–30 and compound ratio manipulations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Archimedes' enumerated sphere/cone/segment problems (goals)
rubrics_metrics.description: List of classical construction/ratio problems: e.g., find plane area equal to a sphere's surface; given a cone/cylinder find an equal sphere; cut a sphere to get segments in assigned content or surface ratios; make one sphere segment similar to another; given two segments find a segment similar to one and equal in content to the other; cut a segment so its ratio to a cone exceeds 3:2; and more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are stated goals/problems Archimedes addresses or corrects (some previously claimed results were wrong). They frame subsequent propositions and motivate the conoid/spheroid results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition 1 (spiral generation)
rubrics_metrics.description: A straight line revolving uniformly about one fixed extremity while a point moves uniformly along that line from the fixed extremity describes a spiral in the plane.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This defines the Archimedean spiral as generated by uniform angular motion of a line together with uniform linear motion from the origin along the line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition 2 (origin of the spiral)
rubrics_metrics.description: The fixed extremity of the revolving straight line is called the origin of the spiral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terminology for subsequent propositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition 3 (initial line)
rubrics_metrics.description: The initial position of the straight line from which the revolution starts is called the initial line of the revolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to locate arcs and construct comparisons between arcs and lengths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition 4 (first, second distances)
rubrics_metrics.description: The length the point moving along the straight line describes in one revolution is the first distance; the analogous length in the second revolution is the second distance, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These distances serve as radii for the 'first circle', 'second circle', etc., and are used in area comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition 5 (first, second areas)
rubrics_metrics.description: The area bounded by the spiral made in the first revolution and the first distance is the first area; similarly for the second and later revolutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows statement of proportional area results across revolutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition 6 (forward and backward sides)
rubrics_metrics.description: From the origin, any drawn line has the forward side (in direction of revolution) and the backward side (opposite direction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to determine whether radii-vectors are larger or smaller on one side of a radius and for tangent-angle arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition 7 (first, second circles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Circle centered at origin with radius equal to the first distance is the first circle; twice that radius is the second circle, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These circles serve as loci to relate arcs to distances along the generating line; their circumferences (denoted c, 2c, ...) appear in formulae.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 1 (proportionality of lengths to times)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a point moves uniformly along any line, then two lengths taken on it will be proportional to the times taken to describe them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proved by taking equimultiples of lengths and corresponding times (Euclidean-style proportionality argument). Basis for many subsequent ratio arguments involving uniform motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 2 (simultaneous uniform motions proportionality)
rubrics_metrics.description: If two points move uniformly along two different lines and pairs of lengths on those lines are described in equal times, the corresponding lengths are proportional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct consequence of Prop. 1, used to compare lengths described under uniform motions on different generators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 3 (line longer than sum of circle circumferences)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given any finite number of circles, one can construct a straight line greater than the sum of all their circumferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct by describing polygons about each circle and summing polygon perimeters to get a straight line greater than the total circumferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 4 (intermediate straight line between two unequal lines)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given two unequal lines (a straight line and a circle circumference), it is possible to find a straight line that lies between them in length (less than the greater, greater than the lesser).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses the Lemma on making the excess exceed any given magnitude by repeated addition; divide the longer line into n equal parts and add one part to the shorter to get intermediate length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 5 (construction relative to a tangent and circumference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a circle (center O) and its tangent at A, one can draw from O a line OPF meeting the circle in P and the tangent in F such that TP : OP relates by a prescribed inequality to a given circumference parameter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: choose a straight line D greater than any reference circumference, draw parallels and chosen segments to set up similar triangles to obtain the required proportional relation; used to build auxiliary lines for later tangent/spiral arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 6 (construction for ratio less than BM:MO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given circle O, chord AB (less than diameter) and OM perpendicular to AB, one can draw a line OFP meeting AB in F and circle in P so that OP:PF (or a related ratio) matches any given ratio D:E less than BM:MO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct OH parallel to AB and use similarity of triangles (BM:MO = OB:BT) and placement of a segment PH chosen equal to a designed length to get the required ratio; the Greek construction step 'let PH be placed' (neusis) is assumed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 7 (construction for ratio greater than BM:MO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Analogous to Prop. 6 but achievable when D:E is any given ratio greater than BM:MO: construct OPF meeting circle in P and AB produced in F such that required ratio holds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similar technique with neusis placement of an auxiliary line; differs in the inequality direction and geometric placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 8 (construction involving tangent and chord for ratio less than BM:MO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given circle center O, chord AB, its tangent at B, and perpendicular OM, one can draw from O a line OFP meeting chord AB in F, the circle in P, and the tangent in G such that PE:EG meets any given ratio less than BM:MO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses construction with an auxiliary point C on the tangent extension, drawing a circle through O,7,C and using similar triangles/length equalities; again relies on neusis-style placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 9 (construction involving tangent and chord for ratio greater than BM:MO)
rubrics_metrics.description: As Prop. 8 but for given ratios greater than BM:MO: one can draw OPGF meeting circle, tangent and AB produced so that FP:BG attains the given ratio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analogous constructive method with appropriate placement of auxiliary points and circles; used to produce lines with controlled angle/length relations for later spiral arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 10 (arithmetical progression identity)
rubrics_metrics.description: If A1, A2, ..., An are n lines forming an ascending arithmetic progression whose common difference equals A1, then a specific algebraic identity relating sums of terms and sums of squares holds: (n+1)A1^2 + A1(A1 + A2 + ... + An) = 3(A1 + A2 + ... + An) (as stated in Archimedes' form).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Archimedes' geometric proof (earlier in the book) shows equivalence to known summation identities; corollaries provide inequalities and extend to substituting similar figures for squares.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 11 (inequalities for arithmetic progression sums and squares)
rubrics_metrics.description: For an ascending arithmetic progression A1,...,An (common difference = A1), two inequalities relate linear and quadratic sums of the terms (stated in Archimedes' geometric form): (n−1)A1·An + 3(n−1)A1^2 < ... and another complementary inequality > ... (full statements in text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proved by arranging terms and comparing grouped sums aided by Prop. 10 and its corollary; corollary extends to similar figures replacing squares.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 12 (equal-angle radii in arithmetic progression)
rubrics_metrics.description: If several straight lines drawn from the origin meet the spiral and make equal angles with one another, then the lengths of those lines are in arithmetic progression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate from the uniform generation rule of the spiral: equal angular increments correspond to equal increments along the generating line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 13 (tangent uniqueness)
rubrics_metrics.description: A straight line tangent to the spiral touches it at one point only (a tangent cannot meet the spiral twice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses Prop. 12 and triangle inequality: assuming two tangency points leads to an interior point of the spiral lying on the tangent, contradiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 14 (proportion of radii via arc ratios, first turn)
rubrics_metrics.description: If O is origin, P and Q points on first turn of the spiral and OP, OQ meet the first circle in P' and Q' respectively (initial line OA), then OP : OQ = (arc AKP') : (arc AKQ').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Based on uniform angular motion of the generating line and uniform linear motion of the point; times to sweep arcs correspond to lengths described along the generating line (Prop. 1/2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 15 (proportion of radii via arcs, second turn)
rubrics_metrics.description: If P and Q are on the second turn and OP, OQ meet the first circle in P', Q', then OP : OQ = (c + arc AKP') : (c + arc AKQ'), where c is circumference of the first circle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generalizes Prop. 14 by adding one full circumference to the arc measure for the second revolution; corollary extends to n-th turn: OP:OQ = ( (n−1)c + arc1 ) : ( (n−1)c + arc2 ).

rubrics_metrics.name: Propositions 16–17 (tangent-angle sign: forward/backward)
rubrics_metrics.description: At any point P on the spiral with tangent BC and OP joined, the forward-side angle OPC is obtuse while the backward-side angle OPB is acute. The proof treats first-turn and nth-turn cases similarly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses comparison with circle tangents (Prop. 5 style constructions) and inequalities between radii-vectors on forward/backward sides to exclude acute/right possibilities for OPC; extends by adding whole circumferences for later turns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propositions 18–19 (perpendicular from origin to initial line = circumference multiples)
rubrics_metrics.description: I. If A is end of first turn and OB perpendicular to OA meets tangent at A in B, then OB equals the circumference c of the first circle. II. For A' end of second turn, the analogous OB' equals 2c'. Generally, for the n-th turn, the perpendicular OB_n equals the circumference C_n of the n-th circle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof by contradiction: assuming OB greater or less than c leads to construction (via Props. 6–9) of auxiliary lines that produce impossible inequalities comparing points/arc-lengths on the spiral. The result ties a geometric tangent/perpendicular construction to the circle circumferences associated to the spiral revolutions.
